headline: Tim Cook meets EU tech chief over Siri AI launch
summary: Apple and the European Union are in talks to resolve a dispute that has delayed the rollout of Siri's AI features in Europe.
details: Tim Cook, Apple's CEO, recently held a virtual meeting with Henna Virkkunen, the EU's tech chief, to discuss the ongoing disagreement.
The core of the dispute appears to be related to the EU's Digital Markets Act (DMA), which imposes strict regulations on large technology companies.
Apple's new AI-powered Siri features, which were unveiled at WWDC, are reportedly being held back from European users due to these regulatory concerns.
The meeting was described as 'constructive,' suggesting that both parties are seeking a resolution to allow the AI features to be launched in Europe.

headline_marked: [[Dish files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy]] due to $2B debt, but services remain operational
headline: Dish files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy due to $2B debt, but services remain operational
summary: The EchoStar-owned company couldn't repay $2 billion in debt due July 1st, leading to the filing. However, Dish TV, Sling TV, and other brands will continue to operate.
details: Dish, the company behind Dish TV and Sling TV, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, as reported by Reuters. This move comes as the EchoStar-owned company was unable to repay $2 billion in debt that was due on July 1st.
The bankruptcy plan will allow EchoStar to continue winding down its wireless operations, which faced "unforeseen delays." These delays held back the sale of $23 billion worth of 5G spectrum to AT&T.

Despite the filing, Dish TV, Sling TV, and other associated brands will continue to operate without interruption during the process. The company aims to emerge from Chapter 11 by the end of the third quarter of 2026.

Boost Mobile and Gen Mobile are explicitly not included in the bankruptcy proceedings and will continue their normal operations. This ensures their services remain unaffected by Dish's financial restructuring.

Dish had previously abandoned its ambition to become the US's fourth major carrier last year, with plans to sell off parts of its spectrum to AT&T and SpaceX. However, according to The Wall Street Journal, neither of these deals has yet closed.

EchoStar CEO Charlie Ergen stated that these steps are intended to position the business for a stronger future. He reassured customers that the company is operating as usual and will continue to deliver high-quality services.

Boost Mobile and Gen Mobile are explicitly not included in the bankruptcy proceedings and will continue their normal operations. This ensures their services remain unaffected by Dish's financial restructuring.

Dish had previously abandoned its ambition to become the US's fourth major carrier last year, with plans to sell off parts of its spectrum to AT&T and SpaceX. However, according to The Wall Street Journal, neither of these deals has yet closed.

EchoStar CEO Charlie Ergen stated that these steps are intended to position the business for a stronger future. He reassured customers that the company is operating as usual and will continue to deliver high-quality services.
